stem: How did the telephone differ from the telegraph that came before it?

stimulus.source_note: Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent drawing, U.S. Patent No. 174,465, patented March 7, 1876, National Archives (NARA 302052). Public domain. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Alexander_Graham_Bell%27s_Telephone_Patent_Drawing_and_Oath_-_NARA_-_302052_%28page_2%29.jpg
stimulus.text: The image is a page from Alexander Graham Bell's patent application. At the top it reads "A. G. BELL. TELEGRAPHY. No. 174,465. Patented March 7, 1876." Below are two labeled diagrams: Fig. 6 shows three panels of electrical instruments wired together, and Fig. 7 shows a transmitter and receiver joined by a wire. At the bottom, the inventor signs "A. Graham Bell."

options.text: The telegraph carried the human voice, while the telephone carried only written code
options.misconception: Background: it was the other way around; the telegraph carried coded dots and dashes, and the telephone carried the voice itself.

options.text: The telephone carried spoken words, while the telegraph carried coded signals
The telegraph was invented after the telephone and replaced it
options.misconception: Background: the telegraph spread before the Civil War, decades before Bell's 1876 telephone patent.

options.text: The telephone needed no wires, while the telegraph needed miles of wire
options.misconception: Background: early telephones ran on wires just as the telegraph did; wireless telephones came much later.

rationales.A: Background: the telegraph clicked out dots and dashes in Morse code, and only trained operators could read them. The telephone carried the speaker's own voice.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the telegraph sent coded signals over wires, while Bell's telephone sent the human voice itself. Anyone could pick up a telephone and talk, with no code to learn.
rationales.C: Background: the telegraph network spread before the Civil War, and the first transatlantic cable was laid in 1858. The telephone came after it, in 1876.
rationales.D: Background: early telephones were wired to each other and to switchboards. Wireless communication came decades later.
rationales.general:
Compare what each machine carries.
1. Background: the telegraph carried code: dots and dashes that only trained operators could send and read.
2. Background: the telephone carried the voice itself, so anyone could speak and be understood at once.
3. Background: that difference is why the telephone spread from offices into homes.
Remember: compare inventions by what they carry, not by what they look like.
